newsitem.title: USA: Japan's Hashimoto hopes yen holds status after EMU.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Hashimoto hopes yen holds status after EMU.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told British Prime Minister Tony Blair he hoped Europe's proposed single currency would be a strong one, but that it would not diminish the yen's status as a global currency, according to a Japanese spokesman.
"(Hashimoto) welcomed the euro to become the second key currency (with the dollar)," said the spokesman, describing Hashimoto's Friday meeting with Blair.
Hashimoto added that "when the euro will be launched he wished to see it start as a very strong currency," according to the spokesman, briefing reporters at the Group of Seven summit here.
But financial reforms in Europe in connection with the euro could disadvantage the yen in global trade, which Hashimoto said he would like to avoid, the spokesman said.
"He also mentioned that with the launch of the euro, we don't want to see the Japanese yen dropped to the status of a local currency," the spokesman said.
Hashimoto said Japan's own financial reform programs would ease the euro's impact on the yen.

During the meeting, Blair told Hashimoto that Britain would likey participate in the first round of monetary union, but that the government would like to keep its options open by meeting the euro's budget deficit criteria, the Japanese spokesman said.
"(Blair) would like to make efforts to restrain the budget deficit within the required standards," the spokesman said.
"He also said he wishes to keep various options open," he added.
